The reason the House has done that in the past is due to "Executive Privilege," which is the Executive Branch saying "we are a separate constitutional entity Congress' powers do not extend into our realm. Which is true but in the case of an impeachment inquiry Congress does get to subpoena and call witness. So you see why Congress has to make it official, otherwise it's business as usual and the normal scope if constitutionally delegated powers to the three branches is in play. In other words, Congress doesn't get to be dicks to the President unless they formally state it due to Executive Privilege.

A couple of interesting historical bits. AG William Barr set the standard for the White House responding to requests from Congress when he wrote that they should only be responded to if accompanied by a subpoena.
